clue.text: Aid to visibility on landing at end of flight

definitions.text: Aid to visibility on landing at end of flight

parts.words: Aid to visibility on landing at end of flight
parts.note: read as aviation it suggests runway lights for a plane touching down; really it is a roof window lighting the landing at the top of a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A pilot's guide to seeing the runway as the plane comes in to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' and 'landing' both look like aviation, but here they are a flight of stairs and the floor space at its top.
explanation.definitionFit: A window set into a roof lets daylight fall on the stairhead below, helping people see.

clue.text: Not on television? Get away!

definitions.meaning: a TV set that is switched off, read as a phrase
to depart or begin a journey

explanation.definitionFit: A switched-off receiver is a 'set off', and starting a journey is the same phrasal verb meaning depart.

clue.text: Freeholder from the old country

parts.note: ye is an old form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A landowner whose family came from the old country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old country' reads as a homeland, but splits into 'the old' and 'country'. Historically the answer was a small farmer owning his own freehold.
explanation.definitionFit: In English history the term named a commoner who farmed land he owned outright, below the gentry.

clue.text: Essential for a chap to keep wine in it

indicators.note: the man-and-wine combination sits inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the chap holds the wine within himself, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a chap is a man
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A fellow needs somewhere to store his wine, so a cellar is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' and 'in' both signal containment: the wine is held by the chap, and the pair is held by the word it. 'a chap' reads as a person, not just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital or of great consequence is essential; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: A property that may have to come down

definitions.text: A property that may have to come down

parts.words: A property that may have to come down
parts.note: suggests a building facing demolition; really a legal term for property that can come down to an heir

explanation.surface: A building that might be facing demolition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come down' means descend by inheritance, not be knocked down: the legal term covers any property that can be inherited.
explanation.definitionFit: In law the word names any inheritable property, which passes down the generations to heirs.

clue.text: Be careful giving odds about reduced villany

indicators.note: the odds letters go round the outside of the shortened word for wrongdoing

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds at the start of a horse race

indicators.note: the word for villainy is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: crime is villainy, wicked deeds

explanation.surface: Someone cautious offering betting odds on a lesser form of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the final letter and 'about' wraps the odds round what is left. Villany is an old spelling of villainy; SP (starting price) is racing shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise carefully, being sparing with money or supplies.

clue.text: Banter is a spurious substitute

definitions.meaning: light teasing talk, as a verb or noun
worthless husks or strips of foil used to confuse radar, a false stand-in

explanation.definitionFit: Teasing talk is one sense; worthless husks, or radar-jamming foil strips standing in for real targets, give the other.

clue.text: Specify how a sportsman shows his style

definitions.text: how a sportsman shows his style
definitions.meaning: a player displays his style in his stance, the way he stands

explanation.definitionFit: To cite something as an example is to specify it; split in two the word says a player reveals his style through his stance.

clue.text: Viewing aid not dependent on sound receivers

definitions.text: Viewing aid not dependent on sound receivers

parts.words: Viewing aid not dependent on sound receivers
parts.note: sound receivers are ears, not radios: these spectacles clip to the nose and need no arms over the ears

explanation.surface: A screen for watching that works without an audio set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound receivers' looks like radio or TV equipment, but means ears: these glasses grip the nose with no side arms.
explanation.definitionFit: These old-fashioned eyeglasses clip onto the bridge of the nose rather than resting on the ears.

clue.text: Pronounced soldiers to be dependable workers

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word for soldiers stands for one that sounds the same

parts.note: troopers are cavalry soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers said to be reliable people at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a theatre company who carry on whatever happens became a byword for reliable, uncomplaining staff.

clue.text: Standard issue for a churchman

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: A regulation item supplied to a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like something handed out, but it means children.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest is a clergyman, especially an Anglican one.

clue.text: Sets of numbers for road vehicles

definitions.meaning: codes of digits that open locks

explanation.definitionFit: Lock codes are digit sequences; and a motorcycle with sidecar is called by the same word in Britain.

clue.text: Instinct for selecting excellence shown by head of Louvre in exhibition

indicators.note: the leading letter of the gallery's name goes inside the word for a show

parts.note: a fair is an exhibition or trade show

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Louvre's director has a good eye for choosing the best works for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of Louvre' is L, which goes 'in' FAIR. 'Head' looks like the gallery's director.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural knack or discerning taste, especially for spotting what is good, is this kind of gift.

clue.text: Members standing round the wicket?

parts.note: sounds like fielders round the stumps in cricket; a wicket is also a small door or gate, and these are the timbers surrounding one

explanation.surface: Cricket fielders gathered round the stumps.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicket is the set of stumps, but the word also means a small door or gate; 'members' are the wooden pieces surrounding such an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The jambs and lintel that surround a doorway form the structure into which a door is hung.

clue.text: Full authority to cancel the bar after trouble

indicators.note: the letters of the words are thrown into disorder, as if troubled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A licensing authority with power to shut the pub after a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after trouble' is the anagram signal: 'cancel the bar' looks like a licensing order, but its twelve letters are simply reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase, literally a blank card, it means unlimited freedom or authority to act.

clue.text: Have canal diverted in the fall

indicators.note: a diverted waterway changes course, so these letters change order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A waterway rerouted in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges HAVE CANAL. 'Fall' looks like autumn, but it is a mass of snow coming down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden slide of snow and ice down a mountainside is a great fall.

clue.text: Downward path that may lead to better times?

definitions.text: Downward path that may lead to better times?

parts.words: Downward path that may lead to better times?
parts.note: a road to ruin seems meant, but it is a snowy run where racers aim for faster times

explanation.surface: A decline that might, oddly, end in improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downward path' suggests decline; but it is a snowy run, and 'better times' are quicker racing times.
explanation.definitionFit: A prepared snowy hillside for downhill skiing is a descending route where racers chase quick times.

clue.text: Rocky path once leading to the monument

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, so these letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stony track formerly heading up to a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' rearranges PATH ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorial to war dead buried elsewhere, like the one in Whitehall, is a type of monument.

clue.text: Policewoman Kate, woebegone, ordered to find unusual thief

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
split as woe begone, it tells you to send the letters of woe away

explanation.surface: A gloomy WPC named Kate is told to track down an odd kind of thief.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W, O and E ('woe begone') from POLICEWOMAN KATE and rearrange ('ordered') the twelve letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a compulsion to steal things they do not need is a very peculiar sort of thief.

clue.text: Find soil in bed aubretia overran

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of the words bed aubretia

explanation.surface: A gardener finds dirt in a flower bed overrun with aubretia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soil' looks like a noun in a garden, but it is a verb, to smear.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear or daub something messily is to dirty it.

clue.text: The Bulge, say, requires action

definitions.meaning: the ... of the Bulge was a 1944 Ardennes conflict, so the Bulge is an example of one
military fighting, as in killed in action

explanation.definitionFit: The 1944 Ardennes offensive is a famous example of a military engagement, and fighting troops see action.

clue.text: Short item of hosiery with centre of pretty material

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a stocking is an item of hosiery

indicators.note: the middle two letters of the six-letter word

explanation.surface: A small piece of legwear with a pretty middle panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts STOCKING to STOCKIN; 'centre of pretty' is ET.
explanation.definitionFit: This elastic knitted fabric, used for bandages and underwear, is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Ring highly thought of by Charles II say

indicators.note: spoken, so the name stands for the word that sounds like it

parts.words: highly thought of by Charles II
parts.note: Nell Gwyn, the actress, was King Charles II's favourite mistress

explanation.surface: A ring that King Charles II prized.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn was the actress mistress of Charles II, England's 17th-century king.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow tolling of a bell, as at a funeral, is the sound of a bell being rung.

clue.text: District adopting name like the Coliseum

indicators.note: the word for district takes in the abbreviation, adopting it as its own

parts.note: an area is a district

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood takes on a title similar to Rome's great amphitheatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts N inside AREA. The Coliseum is Rome's ancient amphitheatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome's ancient amphitheatre was a venue for public combat and spectacle, an enclosed stage of that type.

clue.text: Donkey engine once used in battle

definitions.meaning: an ancient catapult for hurling stones in sieges

explanation.definitionFit: The Asian wild ass shares its name with a Roman siege catapult, named for the animal's kick.

clue.text: Attitude taken perhaps by one out of pride in arms

definitions.text: Attitude taken perhaps by one out of pride in arms

parts.words: Attitude taken perhaps by one out of pride in arms
parts.note: reads as a soldier's proud bearing; really a lion (one of a pride) lying down on a coat of arms

explanation.surface: A soldier's bearing, struck from pride in military service.
explanation.walkthrough: A pride is a group of lions and arms is a coat of arms: in heraldry, a beast lying down with its head raised is described by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry describes a beast lying with its head up as this posture, one of its standard attitudes.

clue.text: Blow! Harry's in the river

indicators.note: the name goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, beloved of crossword setters
Hal is a pet form of Harry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance: Harry has fallen into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry's in' means Harry is in, the 's standing for is, which makes it the containment signal. 'Blow!' looks like an exclamation of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe out is to blow air from the lungs.

clue.text: Gather to see lambs frisking about

indicators.note: lambs frisking about leap around, so the letters jump into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Come together to watch lambs jumping in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frisking about' rearranges SEE LAMBS.
explanation.definitionFit: To come together as a group is to gather; the two verbs are synonyms.
